subject: Request: Latency & Remedy Adjustment for MediGen enterprise pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MediGen pilot — asking for nonstandard latency SLO + remedy cap

Hannah — quick ask. MediGen is ready to sign the 6-month enterprise pilot (MG-2027-PILOT-011) but they need two concessions before procurement will execute the MOA: 1) relax the latency p95 SLO for the pilot from 120ms to 220ms (they're testing cross-region models and claim variability), and 2) cap service-credit remedies to a fixed percentage rather than our standard open-ended monthly credit calculation.

They are committing to a dedicated cluster (8x A100 equivalent) and an initial run-rate of ~USD 120k/month. Procurement has pushed back on our standard remedy wording — they'd like a predictable maximum exposure on credits and a commercial offset (one-time onboarding credit + a committed discount).

Attachments: medigen_slo_delta_proposal_v3.pdf (customer-requested SLO language), commercial_summary.xlsx (customer-side term sheet).

Can we get deal-desk + exec signoff on a bounded remedy structure + associated credit? I put a suggested package in the spreadsheet: $45k one-time onboarding credit, 18% committed discount for the first 6 months, and a service-credit cap of 10% monthly with an aggregate pilot cap of 25% of billed amount.

This needs an exec decision today to keep the procurement momentum.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive — RedWood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: MediGen pilot — asking for nonstandard latency SLO + remedy cap

Forwarding — Ben's summary below. TL;DR: they want a temporary, quantified variance on p95 latency and a hard cap on service credits for the pilot period. Commercial ask is $45k onboarding credit + ~18% committed discount for 6 months; counterparty insists cap on credit exposure.

My read: this is a pilot with decent committed spend but higher risk exposure if we leave credits uncapped. I want Deal Desk (Avery) and Finance (Lauren) to propose a bounded alternative we can offer quickly — and Marissa, I need your exec clearance if final structure sits in the ranges Ben proposed.

Key constraints to call out for signoff:
- Any SLO variance must be timeboxed (6 months) and tied to dedicated infra + monitoring we can instrument (we should require their telemetry piping into our logs).
- Remedy cap must be explicit and limited to pilot scope; legal will need to add an escape if clear production regressions appear.
- Commercial offsets must be commensurate with our exposure (onboarding credit + discount acceptable if we reduce ongoing risk).

Attaching the customer's proposal for reference.

-Hannah
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks — reviewed the numbers and legal implications. A few suggested guardrails we should present back to MediGen as our approved counteroffer (Deal Desk position):

1) SLO variance: allow p95 latency to be 220ms (from 120ms) for the pilot term (6 months) only, subject to weekly performance reports and a defined rollback trigger (if p95 > 350ms for two consecutive weeks, revert to standard SLO and we get an operational pause to remediate).

2) Remedy cap: cap monthly service credits to 10% of that month's invoice; cap aggregate credits across the 6-month pilot to 30% of total billed amount for the pilot. This keeps exposure finite while offering predictability.

3) Commercial offsets: approve a one-time onboarding credit of up to $45,000 and a committed-volume discount of 18% for the first 6 months. The discount should be conditioned on signed MOA and guaranteed minimum spend of $100k/month.

4) Require dedicated cluster and our telemetry integration (no sandboxing). If they refuse instrumentation, we will not accept the SLO variance.

Legal note: we can draft an addendum to the standard SLA covering the timebox and credit caps. Need Legal to sign off on the precise wording; I flagged with Legal.

If Marissa gives exec clearance on these bounds, Deal Desk will prepare the addendum and the pricing sheet for DocuSign.

-Avery
Senior Deal Desk Manager

Finance reviewed the commercial math. Key observations:
- $45k onboarding credit plus 18% off for six months at $120k/month run-rate equals roughly $115k of gross concession over 6 months (discount + credit).
- With the proposed remedy caps (10% monthly, 30% aggregate), our maximum exposure across the pilot is predictable and capped; I can model worst-case refund scenarios but the aggregate cap is acceptable to Finance provided we secure the $100k/mo minimum guarantee.
- If we approve, require deal structure to include an early-termination clawback (prorated recoupment of onboarding credit) if they cancel before month 3 without cause.

I'll need Legal to confirm the clawback language but Finance is okay with the Deal Desk proposal contingent on minimums and clawback.

-Lauren

Subject: Re: Fwd: MediGen pilot — asking for nonstandard latency SLO + remedy cap

Executive decision: APPROVED WITH CONDITIONS.

I approve the Deal Desk counteroffer as outlined by Avery with these explicit conditions:
1) One-time onboarding credit capped at $45,000 (payable up-front as invoice credit); credit subject to prorated clawback if customer terminates before 90 days (Legal to draft).
2) Committed-volume discount of 18% for first 6 months; requires signed MOA and minimum $100k/month invoice guarantee.
3) SLO variance: p95 latency allowed up to 220ms for the 6-month pilot only. Reversion trigger: two consecutive weekly p95 > 350ms.
4) Remedy cap: 10% monthly cap on service credits with a hard aggregate cap of 30% across the pilot term. No exceptions.
5) Infrastructure & telemetry: must run on dedicated Redwood cluster and stream telemetry per integration checklist — integration must be completed in first 30 days.
6) Operational rollback: if telemetry shows systemic regressions, Redwood reserves the right to suspend the pilot and return to standard SLOs.

Marissa approved these concessions given the strategic value of MediGen (pilot could convert to a multi-region enterprise contract) and the guaranteed committed run-rate. Deal Desk, please prepare the SLA addendum, the pricing sheet, and DocuSign envelope. Legal — please prioritize drafting the clawback and the timeboxed SLO variance clause.

Marissa Cole
SVP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
